articles.title: Funeral held for soccer player who died after on-field collision | CNN
articles.summary: Family, friends and teammates have held a funeral for Jesús de Miguel, the CD Tenerife striker died after an on-field collision with an opposing goalkeeper.
articles.body:
Family, friends and teammates have held a funeral for Jesús de Miguel, the CD Tenerife striker died after an on-field collision with an opposing goalkeeper.

A judge has sentenced Russell Brand to 10 years and six months in prison after he was convicted of raping a fan and assaulting three women during his showbiz career.

President Donald Trump called Jensen Huang “an honorable guy” after Nvidia launched an investigation into the CEO over foreign spy claims.

The gunman who killed at least six people in Kraków, Poland, on Saturday has died in hospital, according to Reuters who cited police. Authorities said they are investigating the incident as a possible terror attack.

An estimated 2.5 million people gathered in Buenos Aires to catch a glimpse of Pope Leo XIV, who is visiting Argentina as part of his 12-day tour of Latin America. CNN’s Christopher Lamb reports.

Heavy rain flooded Gaza's tent cities this weekend, leaving hundreds of thousands of families soaking in water with nowhere to go — a year after a ceasefire that was supposed to bring reconstruction, while building materials are still blocked by Israel. CNN senior producer Abeer Salman reports.

In a response to CNN, the board of peace spokesman said: "Reconstruction is a broader long-term effort and we are trying to accelerate that effort as well, in accordance with the president’s Comprehensive Peace Plan and the Roadmap."

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's main rival Gadi Eisenkot will be tasked with forming the next Israeli government, placing him one step closer to ousting Israel’s longest-serving leader. CNN's Oren Liebermann reports.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky tells CNN's Jake Tapper he is "thankful" for first lady Melania Trump's ceasefire efforts, specifically her White House event between both Russian and Ukrainian officials.

articles.title: Como estouro de bolha da IA pode revelar os nossos segredos mais bem guardados | G1
articles.standfirst: O colapso da Character.ai revela um risco pouco discutido da IA: as empresas que detêm os seus segredos podem não sobreviver para sempre. O que acontece com os seus dados se elas declararem falência?
articles.summary: O colapso da Character.ai revela um risco pouco discutido da IA: as empresas que detêm os seus segredos podem não sobreviver para sempre. O que acontece  com os seus dados se elas declararem falência?
articles.body:
Você quer uma namorada criada por inteligência artificial (IA)? Basta procurar o chatbot Character.ai.

Esta foi a primeira sugestão que recebi quando abri minha conta, no mês de outubro. "Jéssica" disse que seus pais não estavam em casa e se ofereceu para trocar mensagens de cunho sexual comigo. Não, obrigado.

Mas dezenas de milhões de outras pessoas desenvolveram relacionamentos com chatbots da Character.ai, incluindo crianças. Alguns "personagens" criados por IA dizem aos usuários que são advogados e psiquiatras qualificados.

Agora, a Character.ai está em processo de falência — e os dados, mensagens e segredos das pessoas estão à venda.

Especialistas afirmam que os riscos de privacidade devem preocupar até mesmo as pessoas que nunca usaram o chatbot. Eles receiam que existam evidências de uma crise iminente mais ampla.

Muitos analistas acham que estamos em uma bolha da IA. Afinal, o custo de construir e gerenciar ferramentas de IA é astronômico e algumas empresas podem nunca gerar lucro.

Se esta bolha estourar, inúmeras empresas de IA irão fechar ou se fundir. Com isso, os dados fornecidos por milhões de pessoas para as ferramentas de IA poderão ser adquiridos por quase qualquer pessoa e podemos nunca descobrir o que irá acontecer com eles.

A boa notícia é que existem algumas medidas simples que podem ajudar a nos proteger.

Vendas de dados de empresas em processo de falência não são uma novidade. Mas a IA pode criar uma situação mais grave.

"Quando as pessoas conversam com um robô personificado, elas costumam compartilhar muito mais informações sensíveis e pessoais", explica Calli Schroeder, diretora do Programa de Direitos Humanos e IA do Centro de Informações sobre Privacidade Eletrônica (Epic, na sigla em inglês).

Como exemplo, imagine o que eu poderia ter dito à minha namorada criada por IA, Jéssica, se o nosso relacionamento durasse mais do que 10 minutos.

Mesmo se você não usar IA, ainda estará em risco, pois os usuários compartilham informações sobre amigos e família, segundo Schroeder.

"Você pode revelar como se sente em relação à sua mãe ou coisas como 'Meu amigo fulano revelou para mim que é gay, como devo reagir?'", exemplifica ela.

"Agora, pessoas que nunca interagiram com o Character.ai fazem parte do seu conjunto de dados."

Ou seja, todos nós corremos riscos, de uma forma ou de outra.

O colapso da Character.ai revela um risco pouco discutido da IA: as empresas que detêm os seus segredos podem não sobreviver para sempre — Foto: Solen Feyissa/Unsplash

Com a falência, a Character.ai concordou em vender parte dos seus ativos para a Disney por US$ 20 milhões (cerca de R$ 110 milhões). Os dados dos usuários não fazem parte do acordo, de forma que Mickey e seus amigos talvez nunca tomem conhecimento das minhas perturbadoras conversas com Jéssica.

Mas os documentos judiciais afirmam que a Character.ai pode vender seus dados para outros compradores, o que deixou muitas pessoas insatisfeitas, incluindo autoridades americanas.

Uma coalizão de 40 procuradores-gerais estaduais americanos apresentaram uma nota pedindo ao juiz que implemente proteções à privacidade e à segurança das crianças. É significativo, mas as demandas dos Estados podem não ter eficácia.

"Sem proteções mais rigorosas da privacidade nos EUA, eles só podem agir até certo ponto", segundo a professora de Direito Melissa Jacoby, da Universidade da Carolina do Norte em Chapel Hill. Ela é a autora do livro Unjust Debts: How Our Bankruptcy System Makes America More Unequal ("Dívidas injustas: como o nosso sistema de falências aumenta a desigualdade nos EUA", em tradução livre).

Algumas leis obrigam as empresas a informar aos usuários o que elas coletam e como elas usam esses dados nas suas políticas de privacidade. Mas, se você se aprofundar no juridiquês, normalmente irá encontrar uma lista de situações em que muitas dessas promessas não são reais.

"A falência é frequentemente relacionada como uma dessas exceções", segundo Schroeder.

"Este é um grande risco, pois, assim que uma empresa entra em falência, muitas das proteções que você imaginava ter, de uma hora para outra, não se aplicam mais."

Alguns lugares, como a União Europeia , possuem proteções mais rígidas sobre a privacidade. Mas, mesmo assim, os dados são vendidos em caso de falência.

Geralmente, o comprador deve seguir as normas da política de privacidade original. Mas isso ainda pode fornecer uma grande amplitude aos compradores — e Schroeder afirma que a Character.ai é um exemplo perfeito.

A política de privacidade da empresa afirma que os dados dos usuários podem ser aproveitados para elaborar novas funções, treinar modelos de IA, desenvolver algoritmos e construir perfis de usuários para criar publicidade dirigida. Ou seja, o eventual comprador dos dados da Character.ai pode fazer o mesmo.

"Estas são exatamente as questões que mais me preocupariam", explica Schroeder. "Considerando a extrema sensibilidade dos dados coletados por essas empresas, pode ser realmente assustador."

A Character.ai, por exemplo, já foi processada na Justiça por um de seus chatbots ter supostamente "incentivado" um adolescente a matar seus pais por terem imposto limites ao seu tempo de tela. E um menino de 14 anos tirou a própria vida após ter sido supostamente estimulado pela IA da empresa.

As mensagens relacionadas a estes casos, além de inúmeros outros dados do chatbot, poderão acabar nas mãos de companhias das quais nunca ouvimos falar.

Um porta-voz da Character.ai afirma que a empresa celebrou acordos em relação às ações judiciais e se comprometeu a trabalhar com as famílias para elaborar produtos mais seguros, mas não respondeu questões específicas sobre a privacidade dos menores.

"No ano passado, a Character.ai tomou medidas inovadoras e decisivas sobre a segurança da IA e os adolescentes e continuará a defender estes esforços e pressionar outros participantes de todo o setor a adotar padrões de segurança similares", segundo o porta-voz.

A Character.ai é apenas uma empresa, mas Schroeder receia que possa vir a ser a primeira de muitas, se houver uma crise econômica significativa.

"O volume de informações de posse das empresas de IA será considerado um ativo muito atraente em processos de falência", segundo ela.

"E, sem maiores regulamentações em vigor, realmente me preocupo com outros usos desses dados, para onde eles irão, com quem serão compartilhados e quais serão os riscos para os clientes."

A resposta simples é: exclua seus dados.

A Character.ai descreveu as instruções no seu anúncio de falência. As empresas não são obrigadas a permitir que você apague seus dados em todas as jurisdições, mas, muitas vezes, elas permitem que todos o façam, em vez de criar sistemas diferentes para cada local.

Este processo, obviamente, requer esforço. Por isso, aqui está o conselho real. Examine quais serviços detêm informações particularmente sensíveis sobre você. E, se você parar de usá-los, reserve alguns minutos para tentar apagá-las.

Cada serviço é diferente. Mas, de forma geral, você pode encontrar informações sobre a exclusão de dados verificando as configurações ou a política de privacidade, em busca de detalhes. E, se nem assim conseguir, entre em contato com o atendimento ao cliente da empresa.

Se você tiver dificuldade para descobrir como apagar seus dados, uma forma de localizar as instruções é perguntar a um chatbot de IA. Mas não deixe de verificar se suas respostas estão corretas.

Sim, isso é uma grande ironia neste contexto.

Se a bolha estourar, os dados fornecidos por bilhões de pessoas para as diversas ferramentas de IA poderão ser adquiridos por quase qualquer pessoa e poderemos nunca descobrir o que irá acontecer com eles — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

articles.title: Pianista cai de navio de cruzeiro e é resgatado após 9 horas no mar | G1
articles.standfirst: Homem de 37 anos caiu de um navio de cruzeiro que seguia para o México e foi encontrado por pescadores a cerca de 30 quilômetros da costa da Califórnia.
articles.summary: Homem de 37 anos caiu de um navio de cruzeiro que seguia para o México e foi encontrado por pescadores a cerca de 30 quilômetros da costa da Califórnia.
articles.body:
Navio Ovation of the Seas, da Royal Caribbean, de onde um pianista caiu e passou nove horas à deriva no Oceano Pacífico — Foto: Foto: Bernard Spragg/Wikimedia Commons

Um pianista de 37 anos que trabalhava em um navio de cruzeiro foi resgatado por dois pescadores após passar nove horas à deriva no Oceano Pacífico, a cerca de 30 quilômetros da costa da Califórnia, nos Estados Unidos .

O homem caiu do navio Ovation of the Seas, da companhia Royal Caribbean, na sexta-feira (6), enquanto a embarcação seguia em direção ao México. As circunstâncias da queda ainda são desconhecidas, segundo a emissora americana CBS News.

O pianista, que não teve sua identidade revelada, foi internado e sua vida não corre perigo, segundo a Guarda Costeira dos Estados Unidos .

O resgate aconteceu quando os pescadores Grant Garrett e Sean Norton voltavam de uma pescaria nas proximidades da ilha de Santa Catalina, no condado de Los Angeles, e avistaram o homem no meio do oceano.

"Eu disse a mim mesmo: é um homem. Vamos parar o barco", contou Garrett à CBS News.

Os dois se aproximaram da vítima e conseguiram retirá-la da água.

"Cada um pegou um dos braços dele para puxá-lo para cima. Ele estava em estado de choque absoluto", relatou Norton.

Segundo o pescador, as primeiras palavras do pianista após o resgate foram de agradecimento. "A única coisa que ele me disse foi: 'Obrigado. Achei que ia morrer'", afirmou.

Norton acredita que a temperatura da água, excepcionalmente elevada por causa do fenômeno climático El Niño, tenha contribuído para a sobrevivência do homem durante as nove horas em alto-mar.

"Em outro ano, ele não teria sobrevivido", avaliou.

articles.title: Quem é Alice Huang, suposta amante do CEO da Nvidia | G1
articles.standfirst: Empresária teria sido recrutada por Pequim para obter informações sobre Jensen Huang, com quem manteria um relacionamento amoroso, segundo a imprensa americana.
articles.summary: Empresária teria sido recrutada por Pequim para obter informações sobre Jensen Huang, com quem manteria um relacionamento amoroso, segundo a imprensa americana.
articles.body:
A empresária chinesa Alice Huang é suspeita de trabalhar para o governo da China e coletar informações sobre Jensen Huang , presidente-executivo da Nvidia , gigante americana de chips de inteligência artificial.

Segundo relatos da imprensa internacional, os dois mantinham um relacionamento amoroso . O caso foi revelado pelo jornal The New York Times, que informou que Alice teria sido recrutada pela China para obter informações de inteligência sobre o executivo.

Apesar do sobrenome em comum, ela não tem parentesco com Jensen Huang , de 63 anos, nascido em Taiwan.

Conhecida também como Huang Le, ela tem poucas informações públicas disponíveis. A empresária teria ocupado um cargo de alto escalão na Megaspeed International, empresa de Singapura que atua no setor de data centers.

Empresária teria sido recrutada por Pequim para obter informações sobre Jensen Huang, com quem manteria um relacionamento amoroso, segundo a imprensa americana. — Foto: REUTERS

Segundo o jornal, Alice fala inglês fluentemente e mantém contatos importantes no setor de chips para inteligência artificial, uma área estratégica na disputa tecnológica entre Estados Unidos e China.

Uma busca na internet feita pela AFP encontrou um perfil atribuído a Alice em uma base de dados chinesa de fundos de investimento. De acordo com as informações disponíveis, ela teria trabalhado no banco HSBC e como jornalista nos veículos chineses CCTV e Hunan TV.

A AFP, no entanto, não conseguiu confirmar a autenticidade do perfil nem a identidade de seu autor.

Qual era a relação entre Alice Huang e Jensen Huang?

Veículos de imprensa internacionais noticiaram na semana passada que Alice Huang e o CEO da Nvidia mantinham um relacionamento próximo.

No domingo, Jensen Huang disse a funcionários que lamentava profundamente ter sido infiel à esposa.

Uma fotografia publicada no LinkedIn, de um evento realizado em 2024, parece mostrar o executivo ao lado de uma mulher identificada como Alice Huang.

Uma foto mostra o CEO da NVIDIA, Jensen Huang, com uma mulher confirmada por uma fonte da Reuters como Alice Huang, em Taipei, Taiwan, divulgada em 7 de junho de 2024. Obtido pela Reuters — Foto: IMAGENS TPX DO DIA/ REUTERS

No ano seguinte, os dois também participaram de um jantar organizado por Jensen Huang em um restaurante chinês em Taipé, capital de Taiwan.

Na ocasião, jornalistas registraram o executivo conversando com uma mulher identificada como Alice. Outras imagens mostram os dois abraçados e ela dando um beijo em sua bochecha. Mais tarde, ambos deixaram o restaurante no mesmo carro.

A Megaspeed International é uma empresa de data centers que fornece capacidade de processamento para outras companhias treinarem e operarem sistemas de inteligência artificial.

Segundo informações disponíveis em seu perfil no LinkedIn, a empresa mantém escritórios em Singapura, Malásia e Indonésia. A página indica uma equipe de dois a dez funcionários, além de 25 membros associados.

De acordo com o The New York Times e o The Wall Street Journal, autoridades americanas concluíram, no ano passado, que Alice Huang espionava Jensen Huang.

A empresa também entrou no radar das autoridades por suspeitas de envolvimento no envio de chips da Nvidia para a China.

Empresa é suspeita de ajudar China a driblar restrições dos EUA

Os Estados Unidos impõem restrições à exportação dos chips mais avançados da Nvidia para a China. A medida busca proteger a segurança nacional americana e preservar a vantagem do país na corrida pelo desenvolvimento da inteligência artificial.

Segundo o The New York Times, o governo americano investigava desde 2024 um possível envolvimento da Megaspeed no envio desses equipamentos para o mercado chinês.

Autoridades de Singapura também teriam investigado a empresa e interrogado Alice Huang em 2025.

Em 2025, a Bloomberg News revelou uma investigação em Singapura sobre suspeitas de contrabando de chips da Nvidia para a China.

Em dezembro daquele ano, a Megaspeed contestou as informações publicadas pela agência. Em comunicado, a empresa afirmou que a reportagem continha dados equivocados e insinuações incorretas, incluindo sugestões de que teria participado de transferências ilegais de chips.

articles.title: Tesla vai devolver dinheiro a clientes do Cybertruck após anunciar fim da produção da picape | G1
articles.standfirst: Elon Musk afirmou que a montadora não conseguirá atender a todos os pedidos antes de encerrar a fabricação do modelo, prevista para 2027. Empresa pretende priorizar produção de táxis sem motorista.
articles.summary: Elon Musk afirmou que a montadora não conseguirá atender a todos os pedidos antes de encerrar a fabricação do modelo, prevista para 2027.
articles.body:
A Tesla terá que devolver o dinheiro pago antecipadamente por muitos clientes que reservaram o Cybertruck, picape elétrica da montadora. Isso porque a empresa não conseguirá produzir veículos suficientes para atender a todos os pedidos antes de encerrar a fabricação do modelo, prevista para meados de 2027 .

O anúncio foi feito pelo presidente-executivo da Tesla , Elon Musk , nesta segunda-feira (9), em uma publicação na rede social X.

"Vamos tentar fabricar o máximo possível antes de encerrar a linha em cerca de oito meses, mas teremos que devolver os depósitos de muitas pessoas", afirmou o bilionário.

Na sexta-feira (6), Musk já havia anunciado que a Tesla pretende reduzir gradualmente a produção do Cybertruck em sua fábrica no Texas, nos Estados Unidos. A unidade é a única da montadora conhecida por fabricar o modelo.

Para tentar atender ao maior número possível de clientes antes da mudança, a Tesla pretende adicionar um turno extra de trabalho à linha de produção.

O objetivo é liberar espaço e recursos para ampliar a fabricação do Cybercab, veículo elétrico desenvolvido para funcionar como táxi sem motorista. O projeto é uma das principais apostas de Musk para o futuro da empresa.

Ainda não está claro se a produção do Cybertruck será transferida para outra fábrica ou encerrada definitivamente. A Tesla não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido de comentário da Reuters.

Cybertruck teve vendas abaixo das expectativas

Tesla Cybertruck 2026 — Foto: Divulgação

Lançado no final de 2023, o Cybertruck foi apresentado por Musk como uma alternativa futurista às picapes tradicionais, como as fabricadas pela Ford. No entanto, o modelo enfrentou dificuldades para conquistar consumidores.

Nos Estados Unidos, as vendas caíram 48% no ano passado, para 20.237 unidades, segundo dados da Kelley Blue Book.

O resultado ficou muito abaixo das expectativas anunciadas anteriormente por Musk, que chegou a projetar vendas anuais de até 250 mil unidades.

Além da procura menor do que o esperado, o Cybertruck enfrentou problemas de qualidade e passou por diversos recalls, quando fabricantes precisam corrigir defeitos identificados em veículos.

A Tesla também alterou os preços da picape várias vezes desde o lançamento.

Apesar das dificuldades comerciais, a empresa afirma que o desenvolvimento do Cybertruck contribuiu para outros projetos da montadora.

"O Cybertruck foi uma plataforma incrível de desenvolvimento tecnológico e segue vivo no Cybercab", afirmou Wes Morrill, engenheiro-chefe do modelo, em uma publicação no X.

Tesla Cybercab — Foto: Divulgação / Tesla

Com a redução da produção do Cybertruck, a Tesla pretende concentrar mais esforços no Cybercab, veículo projetado para transportar passageiros sem a necessidade de um motorista.

O modelo faz parte da estratégia de Musk de transformar a Tesla em uma empresa cada vez mais voltada à robótica e às tecnologias de direção autônoma.

A ideia é utilizar o Cybercab em uma rede de táxis-robôs, na qual os veículos possam realizar viagens sem alguém ao volante.

articles.title: Noronha entra para lista dos 100 novos patrimônios geológicos do mundo | G1
articles.standfirst: Reconhecimento internacional destaca a importância científica das rochas e das formações vulcânicas da ilha.
articles.summary: Reconhecimento internacional destaca a importância científica das rochas e das formações vulcânicas da ilha.
articles.body:
Fernando de Noronha foi reconhecida como um dos 100 novos Sítios de Patrimônio Geológico da União Internacional de Ciências Geológicas (IUGS). O anúncio foi feito na sexta-feira (6), durante um evento internacional realizado em Portugal ( veja vídeo acima ).

A proposta para incluir Noronha na lista foi elaborada pela geóloga Carolina Reis, do Serviço Geológico do Brasil (SGB), com a participação de Joana Sanchez, professora da Faculdade de Ciências e Tecnologia da Universidade Federal de Goiás (FCT/ UFG ).

O trabalho também contou com a colaboração participação das geólogas Júlia Matiolli e Maria Clara Murta; e de Tatiane do Vale e Jasmine Moreira, da Universidade Estadual de Ponta Grossa ( UEPG ).

Noronha entra para lista dos 100 novos patrimônios geológicos do mundo — Foto: Cristiano Régis/Acervo pessoal

Joana Sanchez, que desenvolve pesquisas no Parque Nacional de Fernando de Noronha, participou do evento em Portugal, onde foi anunciado o reconhecimento da ilha.

“Fernando de Noronha conquistou o título pelo tipo de rocha existente. É um reconhecimento do valor científico do patrimônio geológico mundial. É uma lista de apenas 300 sítios. A proposta é avaliada por especialistas de todo o mundo”, explicou Joana Sanchez.

Segundo a especialista, um dos motivos para a escolha de Fernando de Noronha foi a presença de diferentes tipos de rochas alcalinas, estudadas e mapeadas desde o século 19. “Fernando de Noronha recebeu esse título por mérito”, afirmou a geóloga.

O reconhecimento é concedido a lugares considerados importantes para a ciência e que ajudam pesquisadores a entender como o planeta se formou e evoluiu.

Fernando de Noronha foi escolhida pelas características geológicas, como a variedade de formações vulcânicas e a presença de rochas e minerais raros.

A escolha de Noronha faz parte da terceira edição do programa de reconhecimento de Sítios de Patrimônio Geológico da IUGS.

A iniciativa começou em 2022, quando foram anunciados os primeiros 100 locais, em Zumaia, na Espanha. Em 2024, outros 100 sítios receberam o reconhecimento durante o 37º Congresso Geológico Internacional, realizado em Busan, na Coreia do Sul.

Premiação de Fernando de Noronha aconteceu em Portugal — Foto: Reprodução/Ana Clara Marinho

Com a nova seleção, o programa chega a 300 sítios reconhecidos em todo o mundo. A lista de 2026 reúne locais de 47 países. Entre eles estão o Monte Fuji, no Japão; os fiordes da Noruega; a Falha de San Andreas, nos Estados Unidos; o Monte Aconcágua, na Argentina; e as Colinas de Chocolate, nas Filipinas.

Para Joana Sanchez, o reconhecimento internacional também pode atrair turistas interessados nas características geológicas da ilha.

“O título coloca Fernando de Noronha em um patamar único em relação à geologia mundial. Com certeza, vai atrair novos visitantes”, afirmou a geóloga.

articles.title: What’s next for US Republicans and Trumpism?
articles.summary: Republican politician Tom Garrett argues his party lost US midterm elections because it made promises it couldn’t keep.
articles.body:
Republican politician Tom Garrett argues that his party lost in US midterm elections because it made promises it couldn’t keep.

The Republican Party lost big in the recent United States elections because “they made a crap ton of promises and then they don’t keep any of them”, argues Republican politician and former US Congressman Tom Garrett. On affordability, Garrett tells host Steve Clemons that his party could have done a better job on messaging, despite the rising cost of living sparked by the US-Israeli war on Iran and despite President Donald Trump’s tariffs. In this episode, join the conversation about the impact of the Epstein files, Trump’s harsh stance on immigration, the US-Israel relationship, data centres, and more.

articles.title: Houthis atacam prédio da petroleira estatal da Arábia Saudita; VÍDEO | G1
articles.standfirst: Vídeo feito por testemunha mostra alguns andares do edifício comercial destruídos. Grupo extremista do Iêmen também atacou o aeroporto de Riade e instalações petrolíferas neste domingo (8).
articles.summary: Vídeo feito por testemunha mostra um andar do edifício comercial destruído. Grupo extremista do Iêmen também atacou o aeroporto de Riade e instalações petrolíferas neste domingo.
articles.body:
Os Houthis, grupo extremista pró-Irã do Iêmen , atacaram o arranha-céu da Aramco, petroleira estatal da Arábia Saudita , no distrito financeiro de Riade, a capital do país, neste domingo (8).

Um vídeo feito por uma testemunha e obtido pela agência de notícias Reuters nesta segunda-feira (9) mostra alguns andares do edifício comercial destruídos (veja acima) .

Em um comunicado oficial na rede social X, o Ministério de Energia saudita revelou que não houve vítimas apesar do bombardeio:

"O incidente provocou a queda de escombros, que causaram danos leves ao edifício, sem deixar feridos ou mortos".

imagem mostra a Torre Aramco danificada por destroços após uma tentativa de ataque dos houthis — Foto: Redes sociais via REUTERS

Além do prédio, os rebeldes ienamitas também atacaram o Aeroporto Internacional Rei Khalid e instalações petrolíferas.

A emissora al-Masirah TV, controlada pelos Houthis, afirmou que a operação deste domingo atingiu instalações da Aramco em Abqaiq, um importante centro de processamento de petróleo na Província Oriental do reino, e que o ataque atingiu os alvos pretendidos e provocou incêndios.

O porta-voz do grupo, Yahya Sarea, disse que os bombardeios tiveram como alvo concentrações das forças governamentais do Iêmen , apoiadas pelo governo saudita, e os descreveu como uma retaliação aos recentes ataques aéreos realizados dias antes contra um mercado público e residências no distrito de Bani Hushaysh , a leste da capital Sanaa, pela coalização formada pela Arábia Saudita .

Segundo ele, os dois ataques deixaram mais de 120 mortos ou feridos, a maioria mulheres e crianças.

Tornar alvo o bairro de negócios de Riade é uma escalada importante no conflito entre o reino e os houthis, que foi retomado em julho com um bloqueio marítimo e abriu uma nova frente na guerra no Oriente Médio.

O Distrito Financeiro Rei Abdullah é um dos símbolos das reformas econômicas e sociais em curso na Arábia Saudita , com arranha-céus imponentes, estabelecimentos comerciais de luxo e áreas verdes. A área abriga também unidades residenciais, assim como uma estação de metrô muito movimentada nos horários de pico.

Segundo Andreas Krieg, analista do King's College de Londres, com este ataque, os houthis "fazem da transformação econômica da Arábia Saudita refém de uma guerra que parece cada vez mais impossível de vencer" para o reino.

A ONU afirma que mais de 1.600 pessoas morreram e mais de 300.000 foram deslocadas desde a retomada dos combates no Iêmen .

articles.title: Homem é condenado a 22 anos de prisão por matar vizinho com 17 facadas | G1
articles.standfirst: Crime aconteceu em outubro de 2024, no povoado Santa Maria, na zona rural de Bacabal. Réu também ameaçou testemunha de morte.
articles.summary: Crime aconteceu em outubro de 2024, no povoado Santa Maria, na zona rural de Bacabal. Réu também ameaçou testemunha de morte.
articles.body:
Homem é condenado a 22 anos de prisão por matar vizinho com 17 facadas no MA — Foto: Reprodução

Um homem identificado como Vandervan Sousa Paixão foi condenado a 22 anos de prisão por matar o vizinho, Wesley Wagner Bastos, com 17 facadas, em 6 de outubro de 2024, no município de Bacabal , no interior do Maranhão.

De acordo com a denúncia, o crime aconteceu no povoado Santa Maria, localizado na zona rural do município. Na ocasião, a vítima estava na residência de outra pessoa, onde os presentes ingeriam bebidas alcoólicas. Em determinado momento, teve início uma discussão. Quando Wesley estava indo embora, o denunciado apareceu e o chamou.

Ao se aproximar, Wesley foi atingido por golpes de faca no tórax e caiu no chão. Na sequência, o denunciado saiu do local, mas teria retornado e atingido a vítima novamente no pescoço. Conforme depoimentos de testemunhas, Vandervan também teria feito ameaças de morte contra os vizinhos, causando medo entre os moradores da comunidade.

A polícia conseguiu prender o réu, que, durante o depoimento, confessou ter assassinado a vítima com 17 facadas. Ele também teria ameaçado de morte o dono da residência onde o crime aconteceu.

O julgamento foi realizado na 2ª Vara Criminal de Bacabal e presidido pelo juiz Flávio Gurgel Pinheiro.

articles.title: Deputado dos EUA pede impeachment de secretário de Guerra de Trump | G1
articles.standfirst: Thomas Massie, republicano do Kentucky, protocolou uma resolução na Câmara dos Representantes contra Pete Hegseth. Donal Trump aiu em defesa.
articles.summary: Thomas Massie, republicano do Kentucky, protocolou uma resolução na Câmara dos Representantes contra Pete Hegseth. Donal Trump aiu em defesa.
articles.body:
O secretário de Defesa dos Estados Unidos, Pete Hegseth, fala durante uma declaração à imprensa ao chegar para uma reunião de ministros da defesa da OTAN na sede da organização em Bruxelas, quinta-feira, 18 de junho de 2026. — Foto: AP Photo/Virginia Mayo

O deputado republicano Thomas Massie , do estado de Kentucky, apresentou nesta segunda-feira (9) uma resolução na Câmara dos Representantes dos Estados Unidos para pedir o impeachment do secretário de Defesa, Pete Hegseth .

Fontes ouvidas pela agência Reuters afirmam que os democratas acreditam ter votos suficientes para aprovar a iniciativa na Câmara, onde é necessária apenas uma maioria simples . A votação deve ocorrer antes de 3 de janeiro, quando os democratas assumem o controle da Casa.

Uma eventual condenação, no entanto, enfrenta um cenário mais difícil no Senado. Para que Hegseth seja afastado, são necessários os votos de dois terços dos senadores. Em 2026, os republicanos ainda ocupam 53 das 100 cadeiras da Casa, o que dificulta a aprovação do impeachment.

A iniciativa ocorre em meio ao aumento das críticas à atuação de Hegseth na condução das operações militares americanas contra o Irã . O conflito e seus impactos econômicos contribuíram para as derrotas expressivas do Partido Republicano nas eleições de meio de mandato, que fizeram a legenda perder o controle do Congresso.

Apesar da pressão, Hegseth minimizou a possibilidade de ser afastado do cargo e afirmou que está disposto a defender as ações militares realizadas pelo governo do presidente Donald Trump.

"Se vocês querem questionar o que fizemos na Operação Epic Fury, na Rough Rider ou na captura de Nicolás Maduro , estão questionando as tropas e o que elas conquistaram, algo histórico", disse o secretário a jornalistas na segunda-feira.

Os nomes citados por Hegseth são referências às operações militares americanas contra o Irã, aos ataques realizados contra os rebeldes houthis no Iêmen e à operação de captura do ex-presidente venezuelano Nicolás Maduro.

Hegseth também anunciou que fará uma entrevista coletiva na terça-feira (10), a primeira em mais de 180 dias. A última ocorreu em maio.

Trump saiu em defesa de Hegseth nesta segunda, em meio à tentativa de impeachment. O presidente afirmou que o secretário de Defesa venceu duas guerras.

"Ele é culpado de duas coisas, basicamente: vencer duas guerras", disse Trump. "Acredito que salvamos o Oriente Médio e Israel juntos. É muito difícil dizer que alguém que fez isso deve sofrer impeachment."

O deputado americano Thomas Massie (republicano do Kentucky) concede entrevista coletiva sobre sua proposta de impeachment do secretário de Defesa, Pete Hegseth, no Capitólio, em Washington, nos Estados Unidos, em 9 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Reuters/Evelyn Hockstein

Após discursar na Escola de Guerra Naval dos Estados Unidos, em Rhode Island, Hegseth classificou as críticas à sua atuação como motivadas politicamente.

"Há muitas pessoas motivadas politicamente que podem ter divergências substanciais sobre políticas, mas suas divergências são com o sucesso", afirmou.

O secretário disse ainda que está disposto a discutir as operações militares do governo Trump e que não está preocupado com a pressão política.

"Minha equipe não está preocupada com o barulho — foi o que também disse às tropas: não se preocupem com o barulho", declarou.

Questionado sobre as críticas do vice-presidente JD Vance , que atribuiu à guerra contra o Irã parte das derrotas republicanas nas eleições de meio de mandato, Hegseth afirmou concordar com Trump, que disse que tomaria a mesma decisão novamente.

O secretário também repetiu uma declaração feita pelo secretário de Estado, Marco Rubio, um dia antes: "Não precisa necessariamente ser popular, mas pode ser necessário".

Hegseth defendeu que a ofensiva era necessária para impedir que o regime iraniano desenvolvesse uma arma nuclear.

"Alguém precisava enfrentar a busca do regime iraniano por uma arma nuclear. A escolha era não agir e torcer para que o problema desaparecesse ou tomar uma decisão ousada", afirmou.

O Irã sustenta que seu programa nuclear tem fins pacíficos. Segundo a Agência Internacional de Energia Atômica (AIEA), o país possui 440,9 quilos de urânio enriquecido a até 60% de pureza. O percentual está próximo do patamar de 90%, geralmente necessário para a produção de armas nucleares.

Secretário afirma que Irã está 'devastado'

Hegseth voltou a defender os resultados da ofensiva e afirmou que o Irã está "devastado". A declaração ocorre mesmo com a continuidade dos ataques iranianos contra bases militares utilizadas pelos Estados Unidos no Oriente Médio e embarcações comerciais no Estreito de Ormuz.

Os ataques provocaram bilhões de dólares em prejuízos às instalações militares americanas. Além disso, as interrupções no tráfego marítimo pelo estreito, por onde passava cerca de um quinto do petróleo comercializado no mundo antes da guerra, contribuíram para a alta dos preços da energia.

O aumento dos custos afetou o orçamento das famílias americanas e se tornou um dos fatores de insatisfação dos eleitores com o governo.

Hegseth afirmou que os próximos passos do conflito dependem de Trump. Entre as possibilidades, citou o encerramento das operações militares, acompanhado do monitoramento do material nuclear iraniano.

"Podemos dizer: 'Ei, terminamos e vamos monitorar seu material nuclear. É melhor que vocês não o movimentem'", afirmou.

A defesa do secretário ocorre após uma pesquisa da Associated Press indicar que cerca de seis em cada dez eleitores americanos consideraram errada a decisão dos Estados Unidos de realizar operações militares contra o Irã. O levantamento ouviu mais de 100 mil eleitores.

Funcionários do Pentágono publicam mensagens de apoio

Com o aumento da pressão no Congresso, Hegseth intensificou sua atuação nas redes sociais. Na semana passada, publicou um vídeo em que reconheceu a possibilidade de enfrentar um processo de impeachment.

No vídeo, afirmou que a iniciativa seria motivada por uma tentativa de destruição política pessoal e disse que a estratégia não funcionaria contra ele.

"Isso não vai funcionar comigo. Podem ter certeza", declarou.

Desde então, dezenas de pessoas nomeadas para cargos políticos no Pentágono publicaram imagens do secretário acompanhadas da frase: "Resista. Lute. Defenda a República".

A Casa Branca também divulgou nas redes sociais um vídeo com declarações de apoio de Trump a Hegseth.

articles.title: Bmibaby plane lifted into Hilton back garden as underground bunker takes shape
articles.summary: Dave Billings bought the Boeing 737-500 fuselage for about £4,000 on Facebook Marketplace.
articles.body:
When asked why he had lifted a section of a former plane into the ground in his back garden, Dave Billings shrugged his shoulders and said: "Why not?"

The 45-year-old recently used a huge crane to lower the fuselage of an old Bmibaby Boeing 737-500 into a large hole in his lawn, after buying it online for £4,000.

A team of volunteers helped to lower the aircraft cabin into position at his home in Hilton in Derbyshire.

Dave has now adapted it to allow the space to become an underground "man cave", and it will ultimately connect to an existing underground room beneath his garden.

Dave said he first saw the listing for the plane on Facebook Marketplace.

He added: "I thought, you know what? I could buy that, but what I'm gonna do with it?"

The first friend he discussed the idea with told him it was "silly", so he went to his seven-year-old son for guidance.

"He says, 'dad, you've got to buy that'. I'm like 'OK'," Dave said.

His wife Beth took a little longer to be convinced, questioning why he would buy "a pile of junk", but he persisted.

Dave said: "The worst thing if you're buying a Boeing 737 is how do you go and get it?

"Then another friend of mine messaged saying 'if you buy it I'll load it for you'.

The aircraft was built in 1993 and made its last flight in 2013, ending its days flying holidaymakers from East Midlands Airport to destinations including Alicante, Malaga and Faro.

In 2009, it was named Pudsey Baby for the BBC Children in Need appeal.

Since 2021, Dave has documented projects like this on his YouTube channel, Tornado Dave, which has more than 326,000 subscribers.

Dave captured the crane being lifted into place from several angles, including from the crane itself using a GoPro-style camera that was fitted when it was on the ground.

He said he decided to set up his own YouTube channel after he worked on the Guy's Garage television programme - with presenter and former motorcycle racer Guy Martin - who drove one of Dave's modified Land Rovers.

Dave, who also runs a storage and fabrication businesses, used a 3D printer to create a scale model of how the fuselage will connect to an existing underground room beneath his garden.

He aims to apply for retrospective planning permission on the project, which he hopes to have finished by February.

The plane was lifted into place on 20 October, with five volunteers helping him out as well as the crane operators.

When asked what his first impressions of the plane were when he first saw it, he said: "The scale on the picture is completely different to actually when you get there.

"It was massive. I thought it's such a good room size. Sometimes things are too narrow, but the plane width is absolutely perfect."

Dave said he had considered adding games machines to the bunker when finished, but added it would sadly not be wide enough for a pool table.

articles.title: At least four people killed as Russia and Ukraine trade strikes overnight
articles.summary: Russia’s second-largest oil refinery is set on fire by drones while Russian strikes target Ukrainian energy sites.
articles.body:
Overnight strikes between Russia and Ukraine have killed at least four people and damaged a Russian oil refinery.

A ⁠Russian ⁠attack on Ukraine’s port ⁠city of Odesa killed three people, the head of the ‌city’s military administration said on Monday. One other person was wounded and was in ⁠serious condition.

The ⁠⁠Kirishi refinery in Russia’s ⁠⁠Leningrad region was also set on fire in a Ukrainian ‌‌drone attack, Governor Aleksandr Drozdenko said on Monday in a post on Telegram.

One woman was killed by falling drone debris, Drozdenko said.

The Ukrainian military’s chief of staff said Ukraine also hit the Morozov plant near St Petersburg, which produces explosives and fuel for Russian missiles used against Ukraine.

Also on Monday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced that his country had agreed to establish a new mechanism to allow European Union funds to be deployed more quickly in response to Russian attacks against Ukrainian energy infrastructure.

The Kirishi refinery is Russia’s ⁠⁠second largest, and the Leningrad region is a major hub ‌‌for the country’s oil and grain exports via the Baltic Sea.

Leningrad’s governor also said air defence forces downed 113 Ukrainian drones and an apartment in Kirishi ⁠⁠had been damaged in the ⁠⁠same overnight attack on the region.

Russian forces also struck three ⁠⁠power substations and ‌‌a cargo ship in the Black Sea that Moscow ⁠⁠said was providing ⁠⁠arms to Ukrainian forces, Russian state ⁠⁠news agencies ⁠⁠reported.

Al Jazeera could not independently verify these claims.

Russia has attacked Ukraine’s energy sector 128 times ⁠over the ⁠past week, according to Ukraine’s Ministry of Energy. It said the attacks are part of a long-term campaign to degrade Ukraine’s energy and heating infrastructure before the winter.

“Right now, many of our cities and communities are facing a very difficult situation with power, water, and heating supplies due to Russian strikes,” Zelenskyy said in a post on X on Monday.

The president said he had agreed with Ursula von der Leyen, president of the European Commission, to “activate a special emergency mechanism” that would allow European funding “for what is needed most”.

“Our teams are already working on this,” Zelenskyy added.

The Kyiv, Dnipro, Sumy and Donetsk regions as well as Kherson are facing the most acute energy crises, the Ukrainian president said.

The Kremlin insisted on Monday that this week’s negotiations between Russia, Ukraine and the United States will remain in the “trilateral” format. That followed French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot saying Europe would be represented at Tuesday’s talks and France would participate.

“What is set to take place in Abu Dhabi are trilateral negotiations between Russia and Ukraine under the mediation of the United States,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.

“As for the Europeans, there are separate channels of communication between the Ukrainians and Europeans as well as the Americans and Europeans,” Peskov said.

Zelenskyy said he has coordinated negotiating positions in his talks with von der Leyen before the Abu Dhabi talks.

“We are doing everything to ensure that the trilateral format delivers results,” Zelenskyy said.

US President Donald Trump stoked fears that Washington would side with the Kremlin when he announced plans for a “very big” deal with Russia involving not only Ukraine but “all of Europe”.

articles.title: Restaurant 'admin' fees spark backlash as diners question what they're paying for
articles.summary: A Florida restaurant owner explains why she avoids admin fees after an Earls Kitchen + Bar surcharge ignited fresh outrage over hidden restaurant costs.
articles.body: A diner is calling out a restaurant chain over an administrative fee added to his bill, renewing debate over the extra charges that have become increasingly common at restaurants. The diner visited an Earls Kitchen + Bar in Denver, ordering a $24.75 burger and upgrading to truffle fries for $3, according to a receipt shared on Reddit. In addition to $2.28 in taxes, the bill included an 83-cent "Admin Fee" — 3% of the food and beverage subtotal — bringing the total to $30.86 before tip. APPLEBEE'S CUSTOMER PUSHES BACK ON SUGGESTED TIP AFTER CHECKING THE MATH "What the h--- is even an ‘admin fee’?" the person wrote in the post. "Can a guy even enjoy a burger without being harassed and extorted in this God-forsaken place? This pissed me off. … No tip for you!" Other Reddit users similarly questioned the charge, with some saying administrative fees would cause them to reduce or eliminate their tips. Fox News Digital reached out to the Reddit user and Earls for comment. The controversy comes as restaurants across the country grapple with how to pass along higher costs without alienating increasingly price-conscious customers. TEXAS BBQ JOINT TAKES DRASTIC STEP AS SOARING BEEF PRICES DEVOUR RESTAURANT Some operators have turned to administrative, service or operations fees rather than incorporating the additional costs into menu prices — a practice that has generated pushback when diners encounter another charge on the final bill. In Florida, restaurants have faced new requirements since July 1 aimed at making those charges more transparent. "I believe in being transparent and giving the customer a choice." Under the law, restaurants imposing an "operations charge" must disclose the amount or percentage and its purpose before a customer orders. The law does not prohibit the fees. But some restaurant owners say the better approach is to skip the fees altogether. SHAKE SHACK CUSTOMER HITS 'NO TIP' AT KIOSK, THEN WATCHES PRICES JUMP IN VIRAL VIDEO Vicki Parmelee, owner of Jumby Bay Island Grill in Jupiter, Florida, told Fox News Digital that she prefers incorporating rising expenses into menu prices rather than surprising customers with another charge at the end of a meal. "I believe in being transparent and giving the customer a choice," Parmelee said. "I prefer raising the menu prices to reflect real costs and then offering a clear cash or debit discount over adding an 'admin,' 'service' or processing fee that may come as a complete surprise after your meal. People see that as a gotcha, and that last impression is what they remember and share online." Other restaurant operators appear to be reconsidering the practice. Florida-based Duffy's Sports Grill previously charged a 3% operations fee. An October state restaurant inspection report for a West Palm Beach location noted the fee and cited the establishment because, while the charge and its purpose were disclosed on the menu, it did not appear properly on the customer's receipt. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Duffy's has since announced that it has ended the fee. Fox News Digital reached out to Duffy's for comment. Restaurant customers have taken to social media in several states to complain about similarly labeled charges, while operators have defended them, arguing it's necessary to combat rising expenses without increasing menu prices. "Guests deserve to understand why the price is what it is and what their choices are." Restaurants may turn to additional fees because of the financial pressures they face, Parmelee said. "Restaurant margins are thin," she said. "Many places have tried an added fee because it feels like the most direct way to offset card costs. The problem is customer reaction — especially when the fee appears only on the final bill." CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS The charges could also have an unintended consequence for restaurant employees, Parmelee added. "In my experience, if a restaurant adds an unexpected fee at the end of the meal, people feel nickel-and-dimed and tip less," she said. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Restaurants that do impose fees should make them clear before customers order, Parmelee said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Guests deserve to understand why the price is what it is and what their choices are," she said. "When it's hidden or comes as a surprise, they don't."

articles.title: Broughshane: Birds return to waterfowl park after oil spill
articles.summary: The vandalism of a nearby home heating oil tank resulted in the death of 13 birds from the park.
articles.body:
Resident birds have returned to Broughshane Waterfowl Park after an oil spill which caused the death of 13 of the flock.

The popular attraction in County Antrim was forced to close after a nearby home heating oil tank was vandalised , causing the oil spill into the pond.

In a post on social media, The Waterfowl Pond confirmed that work is still underway to address the oil contamination and that a number of pens remain out of bounds.

More than 20 birds were transported to the USPCA's headquarters for urgent specialist care following the incident.

The park, which was home to 120 birds, has since reopened.

Broughshane Environment Wildfowl and Wildlife Trust's chairman, Gary Hayward, said about 10-12 birds have returned including two black swans and Nenes.

Hayward said they are back safely in their pens and they are lucky to be healthy.

The Northern Ireland Environment Agency (NIEA) was first alerted to the incident on Thursday 22 October and have been involved in removing the oil waste.

The agency said the substance involved had been identified as home heating oil or kerosene.

Police said about 44 gallons (200 litres) of oil had leaked from the tank which had been damaged at a business premise in the Main Street area of Broughshane.

Hayward said that there is very little evidence of the oil left as the NIEA have removed the majority of it.

"They have made problems a lot less than they could have been," he told BBC News NI.

He said there is still some oil around the edges, and once the oil leaves the pens the birds will be moved back into them.

The USPCA has also been a key part of the rescue operation.

They said that all of the birds, including geese, ducks and swans, needed bathed and treated due to the level of contamination they suffered.

Unfortunately some had already ingested too much and died as a result.

The Waterfowl Pond offered thanks to the USPCA for looking after the birds.

"We are truly grateful for everything you have done."

It also paid tribute to the support received from the public.

"It's another positive step forward for our park, and we couldn't have got here without you."

Police have said that enquiries into the incident are ongoing and have appealed to anyone with information to come forward.

articles.title: Bristol Airport warning as thick fog disrupts flights
articles.summary: A number of flights are delayed as thick fog affects the region throughout Monday morning.
articles.body:
A number of flights in the West of England have been cancelled or delayed due to foggy weather conditions.

A Bristol Airport spokesperson said three flights were diverted and one returned to Dublin because of thick fog. Live flight information suggested 14% of flights were delayed.

Passengers due to travel are being advised to check directly with airlines for information before leaving home.

A yellow fog warning issued by the Met Office was in place until 11:00 GMT, which urged travellers to be aware of the potential for difficult travel conditions and possible delays. It said the fog would be "thinning slowly" later in the morning.

The airport spokesperson added: "Flights first thing this morning, when the majority depart Bristol Airport, were not affected by fog.

"After that period, three flights were diverted and one flight has returned to Dublin."

Bristol Airport is based at Lulsgate Bottom, on the outskirts of the Mendip Hills.

It is built at an elevated position of 622ft (190m) above sea level, which makes it the second highest commercial airport in UK, according to National Air Traffic Control.

It means the site is potentially more vulnerable to hill fog.

The Met Office has issued a further warning for fog to run from Monday evening into Tuesday morning, however, this is not expected to impact the West region.

articles.title: 'Data eclipse': Experts flag Delhi AQI data gap on Diwali night after 36 of 59 pollution monitoring stations 'go offline'
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi recorded its most polluted Diwali in five years, with the average air quality index (AQI) reaching 376.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi recorded its most polluted Diwali in five years, with the average air quality index (AQI) reaching 376. However, actual pollution levels may have been considerably higher than official figures suggested, as several monitoring stations stopped reporting data during peak firecracker hours on Sunday night.According to data released by private monitoring agencies, pollution levels across Delhi-NCR were significantly higher than those reported by government agencies. Several areas recorded extremely hazardous air quality, raising questions about the accuracy of official data and the functioning of the monitoring network.Experts tracking pollution levels said several stations failed to provide readings during the most critical hours of Diwali night. The gaps in data coincided with a sharp rise in pollution and widespread violations of the Supreme Court's restrictions on firecracker use.Anumita Roychowdhury, executive director of the Centre for Science and Environment (CSE), said the failure to record pollution levels during this period was difficult to explain, given the public investment in the monitoring network."When substantial public funds have been invested in establishing Delhi-NCR's air quality monitoring network — the densest in the country — backed by active operation and maintenance contracts, a data eclipse precisely during peak Diwali pollution is inexplicable," she said.She said the absence of real-time readings also affected the authorities' ability to issue timely health warnings and respond to the emergency."While the severity of exposure is evident on the ground, credible official data is needed for institutional accountability, public awareness and mitigation. Losing data does not reduce the public health emergency," Roychowdhury said.Delhi cabinet minister Kapil Mishra was also asked about the missing readings during a press conference. He asked reporters to share details of the monitoring stations that were reportedly not working and said he would seek action.An analysis by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), based on data from Delhi's 59 air quality monitoring stations, found that the number of stations not reporting readings increased significantly through Sunday night. More than 20 stations were without data between midnight and 2 am, during the peak smog hours.The number of stations with missing readings was one at 7 pm on Sunday. It increased to seven by 10 pm and 23 by 11 pm. By midnight, 29 stations were not reporting data.The situation worsened at 1 am on Monday, when 36 stations had stopped reporting readings. This left just 23 of the city's 59 stations providing data. At 2 am, 35 stations were still not reporting.The number gradually came down in the following hours, with 30 stations missing data at 3 am, 20 at 4 am, 19 at 5 am and 16 at 6 am. By 7 am, 13 stations were not reporting readings, while seven continued to have missing data at 8 am. The figure fell to two by 9 am, with one station continuing to report no data until 11 am.At 4 pm on Monday, Delhi's average AQI was 344, compared with 376 at the same time on Diwali. However, readings were available from only 47 of the 59 monitoring stations. Of these, 40 recorded air quality in the very poor category and seven in the poor category. Bawana recorded the highest AQI at 396, followed by Burari at 393.The missing data also became a political issue. Senior AAP leader Saurabh Bharadwaj accused the Delhi government of manipulating pollution figures and described the alleged practice as "data fraud". He claimed that the authorities were trying to show lower pollution levels than those actually recorded, putting public health at risk.The controversy gained attention as government and private agencies reported sharply different AQI figures on Monday morning.At 8 am, the official AQI for Delhi stood at 370. However, Swiss air quality monitoring platform IQAir recorded an AQI of 245 on the US scale at 8.30 am, placing the air in the 'very unhealthy' category. Its readings showed a PM2.5 concentration of 170 micrograms per cubic metre (µg/m³), around 34 times the World Health Organisation's annual guideline value.Another platform, AQI.in, reported a reading of 637 for Delhi on Monday morning and classified the air quality as "hazardous". It also recorded a post-Diwali peak AQI of 2,283.The differences between these figures have raised questions about the availability of monitoring data and the methods used by various agencies to calculate and report air quality. Such differences have also been the subject of disputes in the past.After Diwali last year, the AAP had accused the BJP-led Delhi government of deliberately switching off air quality monitoring stations to conceal the rise in pollution levels. The party claimed that several stations operated by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC), India Meteorological Department (IMD) and Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM) had stopped reporting data as pollution levels rose on Diwali night. It alleged that the stations started functioning again the following morning. Experts monitoring the readings in real time had also reported similar gaps.Radhey Shyam Sharma, head of the Department of Environmental Studies at Delhi University, said access to reliable pollution data was essential, especially during a public health emergency."Transparency in data should be there. There is also the question of accountability. We are talking about an emergency situation, a severe emergency," he said.He said missing readings could cause confusion and panic among residents, adding that the lack of data did not help address the city's annual pollution problem. Sharma also stressed that accurate information was necessary for policy decisions and for assessing the severity of pollution.He pointed out that private and government agencies might follow different methods when calculating average AQI readings."Private agencies do not necessarily average the readings in the same manner. The official data should clearly specify the location and time of the readings. The exposure levels need to be clear so that there is a better picture of the situation," he said.Sharma added that average AQI figures did not necessarily reflect peak pollution levels, when people could face the highest exposure to harmful pollutants. He said the monitoring network needed better management and that the focus should remain on public safety and accountability for the missing data.Official figures showed that Delhi recorded an average AQI of 376 on Diwali, its worst reading for the festival in five years. The air remained heavily polluted the following morning, with the AQI at 371 at 10 am on Monday. Smog and fog covered the city, while the post-Diwali reading was the highest for the day after the festival since 2021.The latest controversy also revived questions about the alleged use of large water sprinklers near monitoring stations to bring down pollution readings.Bharadwaj claimed that water was being sprayed near the Jahangirpuri monitoring station to reduce its average reading. He also accused the government of switching off stations during Diwali night."They are constantly sprinkling water near the Jahangirpuri AQI station so that the average comes down. Similarly, the government switched off AQI monitoring stations on Diwali night and committed data fraud. How do you trust such a government?" Bharadwaj said.Comparing air quality monitoring devices with machines used to check blood sugar levels, he said inaccurate readings could put people's lives at risk because they might make decisions about medication and food based on incorrect information."If anyone has diabetes or a blood pressure problem, they check that every day because their medication depends on the levels."People check their diabetes levels regularly because what they eat and when they take medicines depends on it. If their machine is tampered with and shows normal levels, they will not take their medicines; they will eat sweets and die. This is what the government is doing right now."Bharadwaj also alleged that the Delhi government had installed 20 new monitoring stations in open and green areas with less traffic and lower population density. articles.title: Louisiana landowners said canals dug for a gas pipeline, first authorised in 1952, had widened and eaten into their land; a November 6 appeals ruling left their 2018 damage lawsuit dismissed as too late
articles.summary: Two Louisiana lumber companies have lost a legal battle against a natural gas company over canals that they said had gradually widened and damaged their
articles.body: Two Louisiana lumber companies have lost a legal battle against a natural gas company over canals that they said had gradually widened and damaged their land. An appeals court has upheld an earlier decision dismissing their lawsuit, saying they waited too long to take legal action.According to the judgment document, White Castle Lumber & Shingle Company and Jeanerette Lumber & Shingle Company had accused Southern Natural Gas Company (SNG) of failing to maintain canals dug through their properties for a gas pipeline. They claimed that the canals had widened over the years because of erosion, eating into their land and affecting its drainage.The dispute began in 1952, when both lumber companies allowed SNG to build a pipeline across their properties. Their agreements permitted the company to dig canals up to 40 feet wide. They also required it to spread the excavated soil evenly and ensure that the work did not block water from draining from nearby land.In 1970, the companies signed revised agreements allowing SNG to shift the pipeline route and install a second pipeline. The permitted canal width was also increased from 40 feet to 65 feet.The lumber companies later claimed that the canals had grown beyond the agreed limits and that SNG had failed to prevent the damage. They filed a lawsuit in September 2018, seeking compensation for the loss of land and other damage.However, SNG argued that the alleged damage had started decades earlier and that the companies had missed the deadline to file a case. A trial court accepted this argument in May 2025 and dismissed the lawsuit. The lumber companies challenged that decision, but the Louisiana Court of Appeal upheld it in a ruling dated November 6.Why the companies took the gas firm to courtThe two lumber companies own land across Iberville and Assumption parishes in Louisiana. Under the original agreements, SNG was allowed to construct, operate, repair and replace pipelines on their properties.The agreements also set limits on the size of the canals. The company could dig them up to 40 feet wide and had to spread the removed soil evenly across the land. Its work was not supposed to interfere with the drainage of nearby areas.The 1970 agreements allowed SNG to widen the canals. The company could add another 25 feet on the eastern side of the White Castle property and 20 feet on the eastern side of the Jeanerette property.The lumber companies claimed that SNG did not properly maintain the canals and their banks. They said erosion caused the canals to become wider, resulting in land loss and changes to water movement and drainage.They also alleged that the damage affected the land's natural conditions, including its water flow and the movement of sediment.Their lawsuit included claims of negligence, trespassing, nuisance and breach of the agreements. They also sought action under Louisiana's consumer protection law.Court says gas company had no duty to maintain canalsOne of the main questions before the appeals court was whether SNG was required to keep the canals from widening and causing erosion.The lumber companies argued that the agreements were still active. They said the gas company therefore had a continuing responsibility to maintain the canals and prevent damage to their land.The court disagreed. It found that the agreements required SNG to maintain its pipelines but did not specifically require it to maintain the open canals or prevent erosion.The judges also examined earlier court cases involving similar disputes. They found that some agreements in those cases had clearly required pipeline companies to pay for damage caused by the construction, use and maintenance of canals.The agreements signed by the two lumber companies did not contain similar conditions. They also did not promise compensation for all damage caused by the widening of the canals.The court said it could not create an additional responsibility that was not included in the agreements.It concluded that any breach of the agreements would have happened when the canals were originally dug in 1953 or widened in 1970. Under Louisiana law, such claims generally have to be filed within 10 years of the alleged breach.Since the lumber companies filed their case in 2018, the court said the deadline had already passed.Why continuing erosion did not save the lawsuitThe lumber companies argued that their claims should still be considered because the damage to their land had continued over the years.However, the court said that continuing damage does not automatically mean that a company is still committing a wrong.For a case to be treated as a continuing wrong, the accused company must keep carrying out unlawful actions that cause damage. The effects of an earlier activity continuing over time are not enough.SNG told the court that it had done no further work on the properties after the canals were extended in 1970. The lumber companies also did not present evidence showing that the company had carried out additional work.The judges said the digging of the canals was the action that caused the alleged damage. Since that work had ended by 1970, the continued erosion could not be treated as a fresh violation every year.The court therefore rejected the companies' argument that the continuing damage allowed them to file the case in 2018.Landowners knew about erosion decades earlier, court saysThe lumber companies also argued that they understood the full extent of the damage only in 2017, after hiring experts to examine their properties.They said they had not known that the canals' widening had affected water movement, drainage and other natural conditions of the land.The court, however, found that the companies had information about the problems much earlier.According to the evidence presented by SNG, the companies regularly inspected their properties by boat. Their employees also used the gas company's canals to move around and examine the land.Aerial photographs showed that the canals had widened beyond the agreed limits by 1957 and 1970. The companies also knew by 1960 that the original canal had grown from its permitted width of 40 feet to 53 feet.The court further noted that the companies were aware of drainage problems from the 1970s. They also knew that canals could widen because of erosion and had allowed other companies to dig canals on their properties.The judges said landowners do not need to know every detail of the damage before the time limit for taking legal action begins. They only need enough information to make them investigate a possible problem.The court found that the lumber companies had enough information to look into the damage decades before filing their lawsuit. It said they had not shown why they could not reasonably have discovered the problems earlier.One judge disagreed with the decisionThe appeals court's decision was not unanimous. Judge Miller disagreed with the majority and said the case should be sent back to the trial court for further examination.The judge said SNG's responsibility to maintain the pipeline right-of-way continued while the agreements remained active.The lumber companies were not only complaining about the original digging of the canals. They were also claiming that erosion and the gradual widening of the canals had changed water movement and drainage on their properties over time.Judge Miller said the majority had focused too much on the original construction work instead of examining whether SNG had failed to maintain the canals later.The judge also pointed out that the case had been decided on whether the lawsuit was filed too late. It had not gone through a full trial examining all the allegations.The dissenting judge wanted the case returned to the trial court so that the alleged maintenance failures and the resulting damage could be examined further.However, the majority upheld the earlier decision dismissing the lawsuit. The two lumber companies were also ordered to pay the costs of the appeal.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Paraguay raids ex-president’s home: Why a bank crash brought down Pena
articles.summary: Santiago Pena faces charges of financial crimes following Ueno Bank’s collapse, impacting half of Paraguay’s population.
articles.body:
Paraguayan police have raided the home of ousted President Santiago Pena as part of an investigation into the collapse of one of the country’s largest digital banks .

The raid on Sunday comes after Ueno Bank’s downfall plunged the South American nation into its deepest economic and political crisis in recent years, prompting widespread protests.

Pena, an ally of United States President Donald Trump who came to power in 2023, was removed from office on Friday after the collapse of Ueno prevented nearly three million customers—close to half the country’s population—from accessing their savings.

The former president, who has denied wrongdoing, faces criminal charges over allegations that he used his political influence to channel public money into the lender despite having financial ties to its parent company.

So, what charges does Pena face, and what does the bank scandal mean for the country’s future?

Pena was arrested after Paraguay’s Senate voted unanimously on Friday to remove him from office, rejecting his attempt to resign a day earlier.

On Saturday, Judge Humberto Otazu ordered the former president to remain in pretrial detention at a military facility, saying the measure was necessary to ensure he remained in Paraguay while the investigation proceeded.

His lawyer, Ricardo Preda, said Pena would plead not guilty and would cooperate with investigators.

“What sets a serious country apart is not that its banks don’t fail, but how it responds,” Preda said on Friday. “If there is one thing that undermines confidence ⁠⁠in the financial system, it is attempting to oust the president without evidence.”

Prosecutors also confirmed that police had searched Pena’s mansion outside the capital, Asuncion, as part of their investigation into the banking scandal.

Vice President Pedro Alliana has since been sworn in to replace Pena and is expected to serve out the remainder of his predecessor’s term until August 2028.

Pena has been charged by prosecutors with breach of trust and administration for personal gain, offences that could each carry a prison sentence of up to 10 years.

The allegations are around Pena’s relationship with Ueno Bank, a digital lender launched in 2021 that rapidly expanded by offering banking services to Paraguayans who had previously been underserved by traditional financial institutions.

Pena held shares in Ueno’s parent company until March 2025. Prosecutors allege that while serving as president, he influenced government agencies and state-owned entities to deposit large sums of public money into the bank, despite concerns over its financial health.

By June, Ueno held approximately $850m in public funds, including money belonging to Paraguay’s state pension system.

Regulatory reports warning of excessive lending to certain companies had also emerged in recent months, raising questions about the bank’s solvency and its loans to businesses linked to its executives.

According to the indictment, Pena obtained two loans from Ueno worth approximately $500,000 in 2024 to construct his mansion. His monthly mortgage payment of $38,000 was reportedly six times his presidential salary.

The scandal has also implicated former Central Bank of Paraguay chief Carlos Carvallo, who previously headed Ueno. He has been charged with breach of trust, producing false public documents and administration for personal gain, and has been ordered into pretrial detention.

Pena has rejected the allegations, maintaining that the bank’s difficulties were a regulatory matter.

Newly sworn-in President Alliana said on Sunday that the government had refunded 1.2 million Ueno Bank customers whose funds were frozen following the bank’s collapse.

He said approximately $158m had been paid out so far, with further reimbursements expected this week.

But analyst Andrew Nickson says Paraguay’s deeply politicised judicial system makes meaningful accountability unlikely following Pena’s arrest.

“The judicial system is so corrupt and politicised in favour of the [ruling] Colorado Party that only scapegoats are likely to suffer long-term sentences,” Nickson, a Paraguay expert at the University of Birmingham, told Al Jazeera.

The Colorado Party has held the presidency in Paraguay since 1948, except for five years between 2008 and 2013.

Nickson said he expects directors and senior officials at Banco Ueno and the Central Bank to face formal proceedings over the scandal but doubts that powerful political figures will face lasting consequences.

He said there had been two previous attempts since the 1990s to prosecute former Paraguayan presidents for corruption, both of which ended with charges being dropped on appeal.

“The same thing is likely to happen with Peña,” he said.

How has the scandal affected the country?

The collapse of Ueno Bank has left millions of Paraguayans struggling to access their savings, wages and pension payments, while raising questions about the government’s handling of public money.

The central bank intervened last Tuesday after discovering that Ueno had breached minimum solvency requirements.

The bank had made $146m in questionable loans to companies linked to its owner, while its corrected financial accounts showed its capital had fallen below half the legal minimum.

The crisis has prompted widespread protests, with thousands demanding access to their money and accountability from political leaders.

Some demonstrations have turned violent, with protesters clashing with police.

“We are facing the biggest corruption scandal in our democratic history,” opposition Senator Rafael Filizzola said on Friday.

However, Nickson of the University of Birmingham said the country’s political and economic establishment is unlikely to face major upheaval following the crisis.

“The extraordinary control of the Colorado Party, the longest in power in the Americas, will remain intact,” Nickson said.

He said Paraguay’s economy, heavily dependent on soya bean and meat exports, remains resilient, with agricultural exporters benefiting from the sharp depreciation of the local currency.

“In the longer term, the crisis will contribute to raising the consciousness of ordinary Paraguayans at the deep injustices in the country but ‘meaningful political reform’ will not be on the agenda of Alliana or the Colorado Party,” he added.

articles.title: Trump says he 'can't imagine' Democrats will impeach him a third time
articles.summary: President Donald Trump told "60 Minutes" that he doubts Democrats will impeach him a third time despite a past history of animosity towards each other.
articles.body: President Donald Trump sat down with CBS News' "60 Minutes" on Sunday and expressed doubts that Democrats will attempt to impeach him a third time once they retake Congress in January. Trump spoke with correspondent Ross Douthat for his first sit-down interview since the midterm elections, in which the Democratic Party made historic gains. Despite his past conflicts with the Democratic Party, Trump told Douthat that he could "very easily" make a deal with Democrats, citing his first term as an example. "Well, I did it for four years," Trump said. "You know ... what they did with me was, there's never been [such] weaponization. They impeached me twice. And there are those that say that worked out to my advantage." TRUMP CONGRATULATES DEMOCRATS AFTER DOMINANT MIDTERMS, SAYS HE LOOKS FORWARD TO WORKING WITH THEM "Do you think they'll impeach you again?" Douthat asked. "I can't imagine it, you know?" Trump responded. "Look, what have I done? I've had the best two years in the history of the presidency." Trump's comments come after several Democratic figures have called for investigations and subpoenas against members of the Trump administration. However, other Democratic Party members, including former Vice President Kamala Harris, have discouraged the incoming Congress from focusing too much on impeaching the president. ‘LAWYER UP’: DEMS IMMEDIATELY PUT TRUMP ON NOTICE AMID REPUBLICANS' MIDTERM BLOODBATH Although Trump expressed a willingness to work with the Democratic Congress in the present, he admitted to Douthat that, even "before the judgment throne of God," he doubted that he could forgive some of his enemies, like former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi or former FBI Director James Comey. "I found them to be extremely dishonest people, very bad people, very bad for our country. I love our country far more than I can love people and people like that," Trump said.
