articles.title: Al Jazeera.net co-founder and cartoonist Shujaat Ali dies aged 54
articles.summary: Ali was an award-winning pioneer of animated political caricatures and Pakistan’s first court artist.
articles.body:
Shujaat Ali, cartoonist and founding member of Al Jazeera’s online teams, has died at the age of 54.

A pioneer of digital cartoons, Ali was credited with creating the first animated caricatures online. He also worked at a number of media outlets in his native Pakistan and abroad, receiving several awards for his work.

He died last week after suffering a heart attack as he returned home from work. He was buried in Qasimabad in Rawalpindi, where his parents are also buried.

Ali was Pakistan’s first court artist, documenting the course of a number of well-known cases using his pencil and skills.

He had recently been working with the Pakistan Air Force, his son-in-law, Waqar Saeed, told the Dawn newspaper.

Before returning to his homeland, he had worked at Al Jazeera for many years. He contributed as part of the founding team of Al Jazeera Arabic’s online services, developing cartooning to utilise the potential of the digital platform.

Ahmed El Amraoui, an editor at Aljazeera.com, said, “I had the privilege of working with Shujaat during the early days of Aljazeera.com . He was a very talented artist, but what made him stand out was how far ahead of his time he was.”

Awad Joumaa, manager of Digital Programs at Al Jazeera English, described Ali’s cartoons as “unlike anything we were used to seeing in a news organisation… He drew everyone from Arafat to George Bush to Osama bin Laden.

“I remember the pride in his voice when he told me that presidents, prime ministers and rebel fighters passing through the newsroom would always stop to look at the wall where his cartoons hung,” Joumaa said.

“We forget there is a whole tradition in journalism where a cartoon could make governments and world leaders shake. Naji al-Ali, the Palestinian cartoonist, was killed for his cartoons. That is how powerful they were. And Shujaat was an incredible voice in that genre.”

articles.title: US agencies unite to combat rogue drone threats nationwide
articles.summary: More than $40bn allocated by NATO for counter-drone technologies as US agencies ramp up measures against aerial threats.
articles.body:
The administration of US President Donald Trump says ⁠it is taking ⁠steps to expedite the use of counter-drone systems to address growing threats.

Several United States agencies, including the Pentagon and the Transportation, Energy and Justice Departments, have signed ⁠a memo to evaluate counter-drone technologies and quickly deploy them to protect aviation safety and address national security concerns.

A statement released on Monday by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said the Department of Transportation, Department of Defense, Department of Homeland Security, Department of Energy and Department of Justice were part of the effort “led by the White House Task Force”.

“We’re taking a proactive, whole-of-government approach to protecting American airspace from emerging 21st-century threats,” said US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy.

“By bringing all our federal partners together, we can strengthen our ability to combat rogue drone threats and keep the flying public safe.”

The announcement comes days after a NATO official highlighted the need for cost-effective counter-drone capabilities, as the alliance has committed to investing more than $40bn in counter-drone capabilities over the next five years.

The agencies will work closely with the FAA and the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to develop new systems that can detect, track, stop, or take control of dangerous or unauthorised drones, according to the FAA.

The agency has approved more than 1,000 coordination requests with the Pentagon and the Department of Homeland Security on counter-drone deployments, the FAA’s Liam McKenna told Reuters.

“There are many systems that some of the security agencies are considering using that we’ve seen before, and we can turn around the process in 24 hours,” he added.

“This summer, the FBI arrested five men accused of planning to deploy drones armed with explosives in and around a White House event that attracted thousands of visitors,” said US Attorney General Todd Blanche.

“The Department of Justice is working with partners across the federal government to address drone incursion threats, prosecute individuals who endanger the public, and ensure the safety and security of American airspace.”

Last month, the FAA said it was barring unauthorised drones along the entire US-Mexico border. The temporary flight restriction bars any unauthorised drone activity up to 400 feet (122m) above ground level and extends one nautical mile (1.8km) north of the US-Mexico border.

articles.title: South Africa detains foreigners suspected of heading to join Russian forces
articles.summary: Africans and others continue to be recruited to fight for Russia in its war on Ukraine.
articles.body:
South African police have arrested nine foreign nationals suspected of seeking to travel from the country to fight in Russia’s war on Ukraine .

The suspects were arrested late Sunday night at OR Tambo Airport in Johannesburg and at a nearby hotel, police said. Numerous reports have detailed how people from Africa and other continents have been tricked into travelling to Russia only to be forced to join Moscow’s grinding war on its neighbour.

Police officials said the suspects, aged between 20 and 26, were preparing to board flights to Russia when officers intervened. The men were detained following an investigation involving Interpol and local law enforcement agencies.

Neither the suspects’ nationalities nor their plans once they arrived in Russia were given. The nine are expected to appear before a court on charges relating to violations of South Africa’s Regulation of Foreign Military Assistance Act.

The law prohibits mercenary activity and regulates military assistance to parties in foreign conflicts, including recruitment and training. Its provisions also apply to foreign nationals in South Africa. Police did not give a date for the accused to appear in court.

The arrests come amid growing concern that many Africans, Asians and South Americans are being recruited to fight for Russia in its four-and-a-half-year-long war in Ukraine, often lured by promises of civilian jobs that in reality lead to the battlefield.

Last September, Amnesty International accused Russia of tricking foreigners into fighting on the front lines in Ukraine in what amounts to “human trafficking”.

Victims from South Africa, Brazil, Colombia, Sri Lanka and more were duped into travelling to Russia to take up well-paid civilian or non-combat jobs, then forced to join the Russian army on arrival, the report said.

In February this year, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said that more than 1,700 people from 36 African nations are known to be fighting for Russia in its war on Ukraine, urging governments to warn their citizens against joining the conflict, and accusing Russia of “trying to drag African citizens into a deadly war”.

Earlier this year, South Africa said it had secured the return of 11 men lured into fighting for Russia. Kenyans and Cameroonians are among other African nationalities to have been killed in the war.

articles.title: Man shot dead inside car; 18 rounds fired, gang rivalry suspected
articles.summary: Gurgaon’s Pataudi: Deepak, 35, shot dead in his car near Sidhrawali bus stand; 18 rounds fired. Police probe gang rivalry; CCTV, FIR filed.
articles.body: Gurgaon: A 35-year-old man with a criminal record was found shot dead in his Maruti Swift near Sidhrawali bus stand in Pataudi on Monday morning, with his seat belt still fastened.Police said Deepak was attacked around 11pm on Sunday and was found in the driver’s seat with around 15 bullet injuries to his chest, neck, hands and feet. The exact number will be ascertained after autopsy. The assailants allegedly fired 18 rounds and police recovered 18 empty cartridges from outside the vehicle.Deepak had four criminal cases against him, including a 2016 murder, and was suspected to have links with slain gangster Ashok Rathi, who was killed in 2019. Investigators are examining whether the killing resulted from gang rivalry or an old personal enmity. The identity of the shooters, the motive and the exact sequence of events remain under investigation.Deepak, a resident of Sidhrawali, had left home after performing Diwali rituals with his family. He was heading towards Gurgaon-Delhi Expressway when the attackers opened fire near the village bus stand. After being hit, his car rammed into a divider, according to police.“It was around 7.45am that passersby noticed the car with bullet marks and a man lying unconscious in a pool of blood. We were informed about the incident around 8am, following which we immediately started our investigation,” Bilaspur station house officer Sunil Kumar said.According to the FIR registered at Bilaspur police station, Deepak’s uncle Prahlad Singh (65) received information around 8am on Monday that his nephew had been shot dead. He reached the spot with family members and found Deepak dead inside his car. In his complaint, Prahlad said Deepak had left home without telling the family where he was headed.A police officer said a large crowd had gathered by the time the police team reached the spot. The vehicle’s right-side glass was broken.“He had called me on Dhanteras saying that he would visit us soon after Diwali. We never imagined this would happen,” Gaurav Tak, his brother-in-law, told TOI.CCTV footage recovered by police shows one person approaching Deepak’s car while he was driving near the bus stand and opening fire at the vehicle. Investigators are examining whether more people were involved and if they arrived on a motorcycle or in a four-wheeler, police spokesperson Sandeep Turan said.A case was registered at Bilaspur police station on Monday under section 103(1) (murder) 3(5) (acts done with common intention) of BNS and 25(1-B)(a) of Arms Act. The investigation has been assigned to sub-inspector Mohammad Zahid. Several teams, including the crime branch, have been formed to identify and arrest the assailants.Deepak was suspected to have been involved in the 2016 murder of Rathi’s wife. Rathi had six murder cases and around 40 other criminal cases against him, including cases linked to the murders of his brother-in-law and mother-in-law, and the killing of his wife in 2016.Investigators are examining whether Deepak’s alleged association with Rathi and the old murder cases could have triggered the attack. articles.title: WWE legend shares the importance of standing for the national anthem, working with US military members
articles.summary: WWE Hall of Famer Goldberg revealed the deeply personal reason he stands with his hand over his heart during "The Star-Spangled Banner" every time.
articles.body: In a world where standing for the national anthem with your hand over your heart has become a topic for debate, WWE Hall of Famer Goldberg left no doubt on where he stood on the issue. Goldberg, whose real name is Bill Goldberg, appeared on NewsNation and told former Charlotte 49ers head football coach Bill Poggi that his respect, appreciation and admiration for those who have served in the U.S. military is the reason why he shows allegiance when "The Star-Spangled Banner" is played. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE "Well, especially in today's day and age when people like to forget history and people don't necessarily appreciate who came before them," he said. "I stand for the national anthem and I put my hand over my heart because there's so many people who have put their lives on the line for people that they don't know just as a job to protect the country. And that, in itself, is a reason to stand up and show allegiance. I cannot tell you the joy that I get out of seeing these men and women deployed and deriving some type of enjoyment and excitement to interact with someone such as myself. So why wouldn't you spread that as much as humanly possible and make it part of every day of your life to try to put a smile on somebody's face and, in this case, a veteran who again put their lives on the line for people that they don't even know to serve their country? "So for me, if I can go out of my way to pat someone on the back and look them in the eye and say thank you and have them understand that it's truly coming from my heart with no ulterior motive whatsoever. I don't care about getting somebody taking a picture of me shaking somebody's hand and posting it and showing what a good guy I am. That's not why I do it. I do it because I can look in their eye and see how much they appreciate it." Goldberg credited his parents, his sister and those who came before him with teaching him "how to be a human being." He said, now, taking care of his children and his family along with "taking care of our military" are some of the most important things in his life. Goldberg played 14 games in the NFL with the Atlanta Falcons between 1992 and 1994. He also spent time in the World League of American Football.
